Ich habe einige Änderungs/Prüfungsanforderungen zur aktuellen Implementierung der Smart-Location-Update Funktionsimplementierung und der Zusammenhang zwischen Signifikant-Location und Häufige-Updates Modi.

1. prüfen: bei aktivierung der notification für smart-updates wird auch notification permission geprüft?
2. prüfen: dass die bewegungsschwellen, server senden-intervalle und besucher prüfen intervalle auch für smarte häufige updates zählen so wie manuelle häufige updates
3. UX: wenn häufige hintergrund updates manuell aktiviert sind / gerade noch aktiv sind dann soll der smart-häufige updates toggle ausgegraut werden. Dieser kann erst deaktiviert werden/ist nicht mehr ausgegraut wenn der manuelle modus auch deaktiviert wurde. Das soll auch als texterklärung erklärt werden (alle sprachen)
4. Übersetzung/Text anpassen "Significant-Change-Modus" sollte eine bessere formulierung haben - eher ap-weit als "stromsparender standard modus" (besser formulieren!)
5. fix/review: es gibt haufenweise Stale Übersetzungen in localizable, muss gefixt werden
6. UI/UX: formatierung/design/schriftgrössen, icons etc. der "Hintergrund Status" Sektion im "Details zur Standortverfolgung" view soll an die statistik liste im oberen bereich angepasst werden - darf sein eigener bereich bleiben, soll aber optisch gleich aussehen. Die "Berechtigungsstatus" sektion soll direkt unter "Geräte-Zugriffskontrolle" angezeigt werden und in "Standort-Zugriffskontrolle" umbenannt werden

     1	# miataru iOS App
     2	
     3	**miataru** is an open-source iPhone and iPad app for privacy-focused location sharing, device management, and navigation through Miataru servers chosen by the user.
     4	
     5	Current project state: **version 3.2**, iOS deployment target **18.6**, SwiftUI app target plus WidgetKit extension, localized for **da, de, en, es, fi, fr, it, ja, nl, and zh-Hans**.
     6	
     7	## Overview
     8	
     9	miataru lets users publish their own device location, follow trusted devices, organize devices into groups, share device IDs through QR codes and deep links, and navigate to another device. The app keeps user control at the center: users pick the server, decide whether history is stored, optionally protect server-side operations with a DeviceKey, and can enable an allowed-device list for stricter access control.
    10	
    11	The app currently supports iPhone and iPad. Mac-specific view files are present only as preview/scaffolding code; there is no shipping Mac target in the project.
    12	
    13	## Core Features
    14	
    15	- Location sharing: foreground high-accuracy updates, standard significant-change background updates, Smart frequent background updates, and a manual frequent override mode.
    16	- Smart frequent background mode: optional two-stage policy that normally waits in significant-change mode, temporarily starts frequent background updates after movement above a configurable speed threshold, and returns to standard mode after a shared inactivity window.
    17	- Manual frequent background mode: configurable distance filter, duration, delivery delay, visitor-history check interval, reminder/expiration notifications, optional Smart mode-change notifications, and low-battery auto-disable.
    18	- Offline resilience: `updateLocation` calls retry transient failures and then persist to a FIFO outbox with configurable retention and capacity.
    19	- DeviceKey: create, restore, reset, and recover server-side authentication for location writes, visitor history, slogans, and access-control settings.
    20	- Allowed Device List: manage device access controls and sync changes immediately from edit flows.
    21	- Unknown visitor alerts: optional local notifications for new unknown devices that look up this device, filtered against own, known, allowed, and ignored IDs.
    22	- Device info: display and edit short device slogans, show security status, and cache location/slogan metadata centrally.
    23	- Maps and navigation: device/group maps, accuracy circles, off-screen arrows, route planning, live ETA, route-progress ghost rendering in standard navigation, focused double-tap navigation, turn-by-turn overlay, haptics, and sound cues.
    24	- QR and deep links: show the current device QR code, scan Miataru URLs, share IDs, and open `miataru://<DEVICE_ID>` links.
    25	- Widgets: text and map widgets use AppIntent device selection, shared App Group configuration, cached map snapshots, and live fallback fetches where configured.
    26	- Tests: unit, functional UI, and screenshot suites are split into dedicated schemes and scripts.
    27	
    28	## Architecture
    29	
    30	```text
    31	miataru/
    32	├── miataruApp.swift                 # App entry, global state, deep links, lifecycle
    33	├── views/
    34	│   ├── Common/                      # Shared UI, map components, route helpers
    35	│   ├── iPhone/                      # iPhone tabs, devices, QR, settings, onboarding
    36	│   ├── iPad/                        # iPad split views, groups, device windows
    37	│   └── Mac/                         # Preview/scaffolding only

    39	├── Networking/                      # MiataruAppAPI, retry policy, request executor, update outbox
    40	├── Notifications/                   # Unknown visitor alerts, frequent-background reminders
    41	├── SettingsManagers/                # Settings, device/group stores, caches, widget sync, cleanup
    42	├── Assets/                          # String catalogs, icons, onboarding assets, sounds

    44	├── miataruTests/                    # Unit tests
    45	├── miataruUITests/                  # Functional UI tests
    46	└── miataruScreenshotUITests/        # Screenshot capture UI tests

     2	- Added the new two-stage Smart Frequent Background Updates policy. Stage 1 (`Smart frequent updates`) keeps standard significant-change background tracking active by default and temporarily starts frequent background updates only after movement above the configured speed threshold is detected.
     3	- Kept Stage 2 (`Frequent background updates`) as the manual always-on/temporary frequent mode. Manual frequent mode is unlocked by Smart frequent updates and overrides Smart runtime decisions completely.

     3	This document describes the current user-facing and developer-facing feature set of the miataru iOS app as of version **3.2**.
     4	
     5	## App Navigation and Views
     6	
     7	**For users:**
     8	
     9	- iPhone uses three tabs: **Devices**, **QR**, and **Settings**. Group management is embedded inside Devices.
    10	- iPad uses **Devices**, **Groups**, **QR**, and **Settings** tabs with split navigation.
    11	- Device and group rows open map views; device map screens can start navigation, open history, edit devices, or recenter the map.
    12	- On iPad, device details can open in separate windows for multitasking.
    13	
    14	**For developers:**
    15	
    16	- `MiataruRootView` selects `iPhone_RootView` for compact width and `iPad_RootView` for regular width.
    17	- `iPhone_RootView` owns the compact tab layout; `iPad_RootView` owns the iPad tab layout and split-view entry points.
    18	- `DeviceWindowEntrypoint` supports value-based iPad device windows via `WindowGroup(for: String)`.
    19	- Mac view files are preview/scaffolding only; the shipping product target is iPhone/iPad.
    20	
    21	## Location Tracking
    22	
    23	**For users:**
    24	
    25	- Location sharing is opt-in and controlled from Settings.
    26	- Foreground tracking uses high accuracy. Background tracking defaults to energy-conscious significant-change updates.
    27	- Smart frequent background updates are optional and normally keep the battery-friendly significant-change mode active until movement above a configurable speed threshold is detected.
    28	- Manual frequent background updates remain available as a second stage after Smart frequent updates are enabled. Manual mode overrides Smart and exposes configurable distance, duration, delivery delay, visitor-history check interval, reminders, expiration notifications, and low-battery auto-disable.

    32	- Users can request location permission again from Location Tracking Details.
    33

    37	- Smart frequent settings are represented by `SmartFrequentBackgroundSpeedThreshold`, `SmartFrequentBackgroundSpeedDetectionMode`, `SmartFrequentBackgroundInactivityWindow`, and the opt-in Smart mode-change notification flag in `SettingsManager`.

     1	# Smart Frequent Background Updates
     2	
     3	Date: 2026-06-04
     4	
     5	## Summary
     6	
     7	Miataru 3.2 changes frequent background tracking from one flat manual toggle into a two-stage model:
     8	
     9	- Stage 1, Smart frequent updates, is off by default.
    10	- Stage 2, manual frequent background updates, becomes available after Stage 1 is enabled and overrides Smart behavior completely.
    11	
    12	Smart frequent updates keep standard significant-change background tracking as the normal state. When a significant-change update shows movement above the configured speed threshold, Smart temporarily starts frequent background updates. Frequent runtime is stopped again when the shared inactivity window expires because no location update arrived or because no relevant movement over the configured frequent distance filter was observed.
    13	
    14	## User-Facing Behavior
    15	
    16	Smart frequent settings live in Advanced Options under the background location section:
    17	
    18	- Smart frequent updates: default off.
    19	- Speed threshold: 5, 10, 15, 20, or 30 km/h; default 10 km/h.
    20	- Speed detection: Hybrid or GPS-only; default Hybrid.
    21	- Smart inactivity window: 5, 10, 15, or 30 minutes; default 10 minutes.
    22	- Smart frequent mode-change notifications: default off.
    23	
    24	Hybrid speed detection uses valid `CLLocation.speed` first. If GPS speed is not valid, it derives speed from distance and elapsed time between usable location samples. GPS-only mode ignores derived speed and only uses `CLLocation.speed`.
    25	
    26	The inactivity window is shared by both Smart stop conditions:
    27	
    28	- no location update within the selected window;
    29	- no movement over the frequent distance filter within the selected window.
    30	
    31	Manual frequent background updates keep the existing distance, duration, delivery delay, visitor-check interval, reminder/expiration notifications, and low-battery auto-disable behavior. Manual mode ignores Smart activation and inactivity criteria while it is enabled.
    32	
    33	## Migration
    34	
    35	Existing installs with manual frequent background updates enabled are preserved. During migration, Miataru enables the Smart prerequisite and leaves manual frequent mode enabled, so the effective behavior remains manual frequent tracking after the update.
    36	
    37	There is also startup normalization for externally changed settings: if manual frequent mode is enabled through the iOS Settings.bundle while the Smart prerequisite is off, the app re-enables the Smart prerequisite on load.
    38	
    39	## Runtime Implementation
    40	
    41	`LocationManager` keeps Smart runtime state in memory only. After relaunch, Smart starts in the waiting state and needs a new qualifying significant-change update before it can activate frequent runtime.
    42	
    43	The effective frequent background state is:
    44	
    45	```text
    46	manual frequent enabled OR (Smart enabled AND Smart runtime active)
    47	```
    48	
    49	Smart activation only happens from primary significant-change callbacks while the app is not active. Smart runtime does not activate from foreground/live updates or from secondary frequent-manager callbacks.
    50	
    51	Battery auto-disable acts on the effective frequent state. For manual frequent mode it turns off the manual preference; for Smart frequent runtime it only stops the Smart runtime and leaves the user's Smart preference intact.
    52

```diff
 version 3.2

 - Added Smart frequent configuration for speed threshold (5, 10, 15, 20, 30 km/h), speed detection mode (Hybrid or GPS-only), and a shared inactivity window (5, 10, 15, 30 minutes).
 - Smart frequent runtime now starts from significant-change callbacks, uses valid GPS speed first and derived distance/time speed in Hybrid mode, and stops frequent runtime after the shared inactivity window when no update or no relevant movement over the frequent distance filter occurs.
```

```bash
const fs = require('fs');
```

```bash
const base = 'miataru/miataru/SettingsManagers/App Settings/Settings.bundle';
const values = {
  'da.lproj': '2 km/t',

};
for (const entry of fs.readdirSync(base)) {

  if (!fs.existsSync(file)) continue;

  const value = values[entry] || '2 km/h';
  text = text.replace('"5kmh" =', `"2kmh" = "${value}";\n"5kmh" =`);
  fs.writeFileSync(file, text);
}
```

```bash
python3 - <<'PY'
import json
import subprocess
from collections import OrderedDict
path = 'miataru/miataru/Assets/Localizable.xcstrings'
with open(path, encoding='utf-8') as f:
    current = json.load(f, object_pairs_hook=OrderedDict)
base_text = subprocess.check_output(['git', 'show', f'HEAD:{path}'], text=True)
base = json.loads(base_text, object_pairs_hook=OrderedDict)
current_strings = current.get('strings', OrderedDict())
ordered = OrderedDict()
for key in base.get('strings', OrderedDict()).keys():
    if key in current_strings:
        ordered[key] = current_strings[key]
for key in sorted([key for key in current_strings.keys() if key not in ordered]):
    ordered[key] = current_strings[key]
current['strings'] = ordered
text = json.dumps(current, ensure_ascii=False, indent=2)
# Match Xcode's preferred spacing for object keys.
lines = []
for line in text.splitlines():
    prefix_len = len(line) - len(line.lstrip(' '))
    stripped = line[prefix_len:]
    if stripped.startswith('"') and '":' in stripped:
        stripped = stripped.replace('":', '" :', 1)
        line = ' ' * prefix_len + stripped
    lines.append(line)
with open(path, 'w', encoding='utf-8') as f:
    f.write('\n'.join(lines) + '\n')
PY
```
